title: Mandolin players and street guitarist Bobo
summary: The only mandolin player he knew, and Bobo, a street guitarist with thumb and finger picks.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: What about mandolin players? Did you ever hear any mandolin players?
The only mandolin player I know is Willie Francis, he's from Downsville.
I never heard of him. Who did he play with?

He didn't play with nobody but him and uh, him and uh, him and uh, Claiborne's brother. Yeah man. Claiborne and his brother couldn't get along though. The one we called Jill. What did he play? The bass player. Mandolin and bass and a drummer.
We had a drummer, he used to use a drummer by a young boy named Milton. He felt around my age now but he was young then, you know.
Did he have any people like in Downsville that walk around in the street and play like guitar players?
Bobo, that's the one I used to start out with. Yeah? He was like a blues singer or something? Yeah, like he was doing.
Yeah? Uh huh. What was his name? Bobo. Fanger, finger pick. Bobo, yeah. You don't know the rest of his name?
I, I never did know Bobo.
He just walk around the street and play like that?
Walk around the street and just pick, just pick it walking. He sing to?

Mm-hmm. Did he use thumb picks or anything? Mm-hmm. Oh, did he use thumb picks and finger picks? Thumb picks. Thumb picks. I'm not talking about flat picks, no. Did he use a flat pick ever? Yeah, the thumb picks.
I got something else. I got something, stick them on your hand. You clapped them on your finger.
I got something else. Do you play that style yourself?
